title: The Day I Became a Team Leader
script: Narrator: [excited] Last month, my manager called me into her office, and I thought I was in trouble because that almost never happens.
Narrator: [laughing softly] Instead, she told me I was going to become the new team leader for the marketing group. I was so surprised that I forgot to say thank you.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I had worked at that company for three years, but I never expected a promotion so soon, especially because two coworkers had been there longer than me.
Narrator: [honestly] When I told my colleagues, some of them were happy for me, but I could feel that others felt a little strange about it.
Narrator: [nervous] My first week as a leader was harder than I expected, because I had to give tasks to people who used to be my equals.
Narrator: [reflective] One coworker, Budi, seemed distant at first. He barely spoke to me during meetings, although we used to eat lunch together every day.
Narrator: [gently] So one afternoon, I asked him directly if something was wrong. He admitted that he had wanted the position too, and he needed some time to accept it.
Narrator: [warmly] I told him I understood, and that his experience was actually going to help the whole team, not just me.
Narrator: [with relief] After that conversation, things slowly improved between us, because we finally spoke honestly instead of avoiding each other.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I learned that leadership isn't about being liked immediately. It's about listening carefully, even when a conversation feels uncomfortable.
Narrator: [determined] Now, when I plan our weekly meetings, I always ask for everyone's opinion before I decide anything important.
Narrator: [warmly] Budi and I have lunch together again, and he recently helped me train a new employee, which meant a lot to me.
Narrator: [reflective] I still make mistakes as a leader, but I try to fix them quickly instead of pretending they didn't happen.
Narrator: [with a small smile] If someone had told me a year ago that I would lead this team, I probably wouldn't have believed them.
Narrator: [warmly] But here I am, and although it's difficult sometimes, I'm proud of how far I've come since that nervous day in my manager's office.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator think she was in trouble at first?
options: She had made a big mistake
Her manager rarely called her into the office
quiz.explanation: She says her manager almost never calls her in, so she assumed something was wrong.

quiz.question: How did Budi behave toward the narrator during her first week?
options: He seemed distant and barely spoke to her
He asked for a promotion too
quiz.explanation: Budi seemed distant at first, even though they used to eat lunch together.

quiz.question: What did Budi admit when the narrator asked him directly?
options: He had wanted the position too and needed time to accept it
He was moving to another city
quiz.explanation: Budi admitted he had wanted the leadership position and needed time to accept the change.

quiz.question: What does the narrator now do before deciding anything important in meetings?
options: She asks for everyone's opinion first
quiz.explanation: She now asks for everyone's opinion before making important decisions.

quiz.question: What has Budi recently helped the narrator do?
quiz.explanation: Budi recently helped her train a new employee, which meant a lot to her.

title: Two Colleagues Disagree About a Project Plan
script: Sari: [firmly] Bayu, I looked at your plan for the new app, and I don't think we should launch it in October.
Bayu: [surprised] Really? I thought October was already decided last week during the meeting.
Sari: [explaining] It was, but after I tested the app yesterday, I found three problems that we still need to fix.
Bayu: [concerned] What kind of problems are we talking about? Small ones, or something more serious?
Sari: [honestly] The login page crashes sometimes, and the payment system doesn't always save the information correctly.
Bayu: [worried] That does sound serious. If customers can't pay properly, they'll stop using the app immediately.
Sari: [calmly] Exactly, so I think we should delay the launch by three weeks, even though I know that's disappointing.
Bayu: [sighing] It is disappointing, because we already told our clients about the October date, but I understand your reasons.
Sari: [thoughtful] What if we explain the situation honestly? Clients usually respect a company more when it fixes problems before launching.
Bayu: [considering] That's true. I remember when we launched too early last year, and customers complained for months afterward.
Sari: [agreeing] Exactly, so although waiting feels frustrating now, it will probably save us a lot of trouble later.
Bayu: [determined] Okay, let's write an email to the clients today, so they have enough time to adjust their own plans.
Sari: [relieved] Thank you for understanding. I was worried you would think I was just trying to make more work for everyone.
Bayu: [warmly] Not at all. You caught these problems before our customers did, which is actually a good thing for the whole team.
Sari: [smiling] I appreciate that. Should we ask the developers to focus only on those three problems this week?
Bayu: [nodding] Yes, and I'll tell them the new deadline is in three weeks, not three days, so they don't panic.
Sari: [laughing a little] Good idea. Nobody works well when they feel panicked and rushed at the same time.
Bayu: [warmly] Agreed. Let's send that email now, and then we can plan the new testing schedule together this afternoon.

quiz.question: Why does Sari want to delay the app launch?
options: She is on vacation in October
She found three problems while testing the app
The clients asked for a delay
quiz.explanation: Sari found three problems, including login and payment issues, while testing the app.

quiz.question: What two problems does Sari mention specifically?
options: The login page crashes and the payment system doesn't save information correctly
Too many users and low storage
quiz.explanation: She mentions the login page crashing and the payment system not saving information correctly.

quiz.question: What happened when they launched a product too early last year?
quiz.explanation: Bayu remembers customers complaining for months after an early launch last year.

quiz.question: What do Sari and Bayu decide to do about the clients?
options: Write an honest email explaining the delay
quiz.explanation: They decide to write an email explaining the situation honestly to the clients.

quiz.question: How long does Bayu plan to tell the developers the new deadline is?
quiz.explanation: Bayu says he'll tell the developers the new deadline is three weeks, not three days.

title: Working From Home: What I Learned
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When my company allowed remote work last year, I was thrilled, because I imagined lazy mornings and complete freedom.
Narrator: [honestly] The reality looked quite different. During my first week, I worked in pajamas until three in the afternoon, and I felt strangely unproductive.
Narrator: [reflective] Without my usual office routine, my days started blending together, and I often forgot which day of the week it actually was.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I also missed something I never expected to miss, which was simply talking to my coworkers during small breaks.
Narrator: [honestly] At home, I sometimes went a whole day without speaking to another human being, and that made me feel isolated.
Narrator: [determined] So I decided to change a few habits, even though it felt awkward to create new rules just for myself.
Narrator: [warmly] First, I started getting dressed properly every morning, as if I were actually leaving the house for the office.
Narrator: [thoughtful] It sounds small, but it helped my brain understand that work time had officially begun.
Narrator: [gently] Second, I scheduled short video calls with teammates, not always about work, just to check in and talk normally.
Narrator: [honestly] Those calls became the highlight of my day, because they reminded me that we were still a team, although we worked apart.
Narrator: [reflective] Third, I created a clear ending time for my workday, because before that, I answered messages until almost midnight.
Narrator: [warmly] Once I finished at six, I closed my laptop completely and didn't open it again until the next morning.
Narrator: [with a small smile] These changes seem simple, but together they turned a confusing situation into something I genuinely enjoy now.
Narrator: [peacefully] I still miss office life sometimes, especially the coffee machine conversations, but I've finally found a rhythm that works for me.
Narrator: [warmly] If you're struggling with remote work too, I'd say this: structure isn't boring, it's actually what makes freedom possible.

quiz.question: How did the narrator feel about remote work at first?
options: Thrilled, imagining lazy mornings and freedom
quiz.explanation: He was thrilled and imagined lazy mornings and complete freedom.

quiz.question: What did the narrator unexpectedly miss about the office?
options: Talking to coworkers during small breaks
quiz.explanation: He missed simply talking to his coworkers during small breaks.

quiz.question: What was the first habit the narrator changed?
quiz.explanation: He started getting dressed properly every morning as if going to the office.

quiz.question: What problem existed before he created a clear ending time for his workday?
options: He answered messages until almost midnight
quiz.explanation: Before setting a clear end time, he answered messages until almost midnight.

quiz.question: What is the narrator's final message to people struggling with remote work?
options: Freedom means no rules at all
Structure is what makes freedom possible
quiz.explanation: He concludes that structure isn't boring, it's what makes freedom possible.

title: A Job Interview That Changed My Mind
script: Interviewer: [warmly] Thank you for coming in today, Dimas. Please, sit down and make yourself comfortable.
Candidate: [nervous] Thank you for having me. I'll admit, I'm a little nervous, since this is my first interview in years.
Interviewer: [kindly] That's completely understandable. Take a breath, and let's just have a normal conversation, not an interrogation.
Candidate: [smiling] That helps, thank you. I appreciate you saying that.
Interviewer: [curious] So, tell me, why did you decide to apply for this position, especially after working at the same company for six years?
Candidate: [thoughtful] Honestly, I loved my old job for a long time, but recently I stopped growing there. I wanted a new challenge.
Interviewer: [interested] What kind of challenge are you hoping to find here specifically?
Candidate: [honestly] I want to work on bigger projects, and I want to learn from a team that pushes me to improve.
Interviewer: [nodding] That's exactly the environment we try to create here. Can you describe a difficult situation you handled well?
Candidate: [reflective] Once, a major client threatened to leave because of a mistake my team made. I called them personally and fixed it within two days.
Interviewer: [impressed] That's a strong example. How did you feel during that stressful situation?
Candidate: [honestly] Terrified, if I'm being completely truthful. But I focused on solving the problem instead of worrying about how it looked.
Interviewer: [smiling] I appreciate your honesty. Many candidates pretend they never feel stressed, which frankly isn't believable.
Candidate: [laughing softly] I don't think anyone truly enjoys those moments, but they do teach you a lot about yourself.
Interviewer: [warmly] Well, Dimas, I think this conversation has been genuinely refreshing. Do you have any questions for me before we finish?
Candidate: [eagerly] Yes, actually. What do you personally enjoy most about working here?
Interviewer: [thoughtful] Honestly, the people. Even during hard weeks, this team supports each other, which isn't always common in this industry.
Candidate: [warmly] That's exactly what I was hoping to hear. Thank you again for this opportunity, and for making me feel so relaxed today.

quiz.question: Why was Dimas nervous at the start of the interview?
options: It was his first interview in years
quiz.explanation: Dimas admits he's nervous because it's his first interview in years.

quiz.question: Why did Dimas decide to leave his old job after six years?
options: He stopped growing there and wanted a new challenge
quiz.explanation: He says he loved his old job but stopped growing, so he wanted a new challenge.

quiz.question: What difficult situation does Dimas describe handling well?
options: A power outage at the office
A major client who threatened to leave because of a mistake
quiz.explanation: He describes fixing a situation where a major client threatened to leave due to a team mistake.

quiz.question: How did Dimas actually feel during that stressful situation, honestly?
options: Terrified, but focused on solving the problem
quiz.explanation: He admits he felt terrified but focused on solving the problem instead of worrying.

quiz.question: What does the interviewer say she personally enjoys most about the workplace?
options: The people and how the team supports each other
quiz.explanation: She says she enjoys the people most, since the team supports each other even during hard weeks.

title: My Worst Meeting Ever
script: Narrator: [amused] I want to tell you about the worst meeting of my career, because looking back now, it's actually a little funny.
Narrator: [thoughtful] It happened during my second month at a new company, when I still didn't know everyone's name.
Narrator: [honestly] I was presenting our quarterly numbers to the whole department, including the company's owner, who rarely attended these meetings.
Narrator: [nervous] I had practiced my slides the night before, so I felt reasonably confident when I walked into the room that morning.
Narrator: [embarrassed] Then, halfway through my presentation, my laptop suddenly froze, and the screen showed my personal photos instead of the report.
Narrator: [laughing softly] Everyone saw a photo of my cat wearing a tiny hat, right there on the big screen for the whole department.
Narrator: [honestly] My face turned bright red, and for a moment, I genuinely considered running out of the room and never coming back.
Narrator: [reflective] Instead, I took a breath, closed the photo app, and said, well, at least you know I have excellent taste in hats.
Narrator: [warmly] To my surprise, the room actually laughed, and even the owner smiled, which helped me relax immediately.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I finished the presentation, and afterward, several coworkers told me the cat photo made the meeting more memorable than usual.
Narrator: [honestly] Before that day, I believed a perfect presentation meant a flawless one, without any mistakes whatsoever.
Narrator: [reflective] Now I understand something different. People don't remember perfection nearly as much as they remember how you handled an awkward moment.
Narrator: [warmly] A coworker named Rani, who I barely knew then, came up afterward and said my reaction actually calmed her own nerves for later meetings.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Because of that embarrassing moment, Rani and I became close friends, and we still laugh about the cat photo today.
Narrator: [peacefully] So although I once dreaded that memory, I've learned to appreciate it. Sometimes the worst moments become the best stories later.

quiz.question: When did this embarrassing meeting happen?
options: During her second month at a new company
After ten years at the company
quiz.explanation: It happened during her second month at a new company.

quiz.question: What appeared on the screen when her laptop froze?
options: A photo of her cat wearing a tiny hat
quiz.explanation: A photo of her cat wearing a tiny hat appeared instead of the report.

quiz.question: What did the narrator say after the photo appeared?
options: She apologized and left the room
She joked that at least people knew she had excellent taste in hats
quiz.explanation: She joked, saying at least everyone knew she had excellent taste in hats.

quiz.question: What did Rani tell the narrator afterward?
options: That her reaction calmed Rani's own nerves for later meetings
quiz.explanation: Rani said the narrator's calm reaction helped calm her own nerves for future meetings.

quiz.question: What lesson does the narrator take from this experience?
options: People remember how you handle awkward moments more than perfection
quiz.explanation: She learns that people remember how you handle an awkward moment more than perfection.

title: A Performance Review With My Manager
script: Manager: [warmly] Come in, Ratih. Please sit down. This is just our regular six-month review, so there's nothing to worry about.
Employee: [slightly nervous] Thank you. I always feel a bit anxious before these meetings, even when I know they're routine.
Manager: [reassuring] That's very common. Let's start with the good news, because honestly, there's quite a lot of it.
Employee: [hopeful] Okay, I'm ready to hear it.
Manager: [pleased] Your project completion rate improved by almost thirty percent since January, which is genuinely impressive.
Employee: [smiling] That's a relief to hear. I've been trying to organize my week more carefully since our last conversation.
Manager: [interested] It clearly worked. Clients have also mentioned that you respond faster than before, and they appreciate that a lot.
Employee: [pleased] I'm glad that's noticeable. I started answering emails first thing in the morning instead of leaving them until later.
Manager: [thoughtful] Now, there's one area where I think you could grow, if you're open to hearing it.
Employee: [attentive] Of course, please tell me. I'd rather know now than find out later.
Manager: [gently] During team meetings, you rarely share your opinion, even when I know you have good ideas.
Employee: [honestly] That's true. I sometimes worry my ideas aren't developed enough to share out loud.
Manager: [encouraging] Your ideas don't need to be perfect before you share them. Half-formed ideas often become the best ones through discussion.
Employee: [thoughtful] I never thought about it that way. I suppose I've always waited until I felt completely certain.
Manager: [warmly] Try speaking up even when you're only seventy percent sure. The team values your perspective more than you realize.
Employee: [determined] Okay, I'll practice that, starting with tomorrow's planning meeting, even if it feels uncomfortable at first.
Manager: [smiling] That's exactly the attitude I like to see. Overall, this has been a strong six months for you.
Employee: [grateful] Thank you for the honest feedback, and for noticing the effort I've been putting in lately.
Manager: [warmly] Keep it up, Ratih. I'm looking forward to seeing how much you grow before our next review.

quiz.question: By how much did Ratih's project completion rate improve since January?
quiz.explanation: Her project completion rate improved by almost thirty percent since January.

quiz.question: What have clients mentioned about Ratih recently?
options: That she responds faster than before
quiz.explanation: Clients mentioned that Ratih responds faster than before and appreciate it.

quiz.question: What area does the manager say Ratih could grow in?
options: Sharing her opinion during team meetings
quiz.explanation: The manager notes she rarely shares her opinion during team meetings, despite having good ideas.

quiz.question: Why has Ratih been staying quiet in meetings?
options: She worries her ideas aren't developed enough to share
quiz.explanation: She admits she worries her ideas aren't developed enough to share out loud.

quiz.question: What advice does the manager give about sharing ideas?
options: Speak up even when only seventy percent sure
Write ideas down instead of speaking
quiz.explanation: The manager encourages her to speak up even when she's only seventy percent sure.

title: Planning the Office Farewell Party
script: Nadia: [energetic] Yusuf, we only have four days before Pak Anton's last day, and we haven't planned anything for his farewell yet.
Yusuf: [surprised] Really? I thought someone from HR was organizing it already.
Nadia: [sighing] Apparently not. I asked this morning, and they said it wasn't officially their responsibility this time.
Yusuf: [determined] Okay, then let's plan it ourselves, because Pak Anton has worked here for twelve years. He deserves a proper send-off.
Nadia: [thoughtful] Agreed. Should we do something simple, like cake in the meeting room, or something bigger?
Yusuf: [considering] I think simple is better, since we don't have much time to organize a big event anyway.
Nadia: [nodding] That makes sense. I'll order a cake tomorrow morning, so it's ready in time.
Yusuf: [helpful] I can collect money from everyone for a gift, although some people might already be traveling this week.
Nadia: [thoughtful] True, but even a small collection is better than nothing. What gift are you thinking of?
Yusuf: [smiling] He mentioned once that he wants to start gardening after retirement, so maybe gardening tools?
Nadia: [pleased] That's actually perfect. He talks about his future garden almost every week during lunch.
Yusuf: [thoughtful] Should we also ask people to write short messages? He always says he'll miss the team the most.
Nadia: [warmly] Yes, let's create a card and pass it around the office quietly, so it's a surprise on his last day.
Yusuf: [practical] I'll handle the card, and you handle the cake and the gift, since you already started that.
Nadia: [confirming] Sounds good. What time should the party start on Friday?
Yusuf: [thoughtful] Maybe around four in the afternoon, right before people usually start leaving for the weekend.
Nadia: [agreeing] Perfect timing. I'll send a quiet message to everyone except Pak Anton, obviously.
Yusuf: [warmly] This is going to mean a lot to him, even if it's small. Twelve years deserves at least a proper goodbye.
Nadia: [smiling] Definitely. Let's meet again tomorrow morning to check everything is ready before Friday arrives.

quiz.question: How many days do Nadia and Yusuf have before Pak Anton's last day?
quiz.explanation: Nadia says they only have four days before Pak Anton's last day.

quiz.question: How long has Pak Anton worked at the company?
quiz.explanation: Yusuf mentions Pak Anton has worked at the company for twelve years.

quiz.question: What gift idea does Yusuf suggest?
quiz.explanation: Yusuf suggests gardening tools because Pak Anton wants to start gardening after retirement.

quiz.question: What does Nadia want to create in addition to cake and a gift?
options: A card with short messages from the team
quiz.explanation: Nadia suggests creating a card and passing it around for people to write short messages.

quiz.question: What time do they plan to start the party on Friday?
quiz.explanation: They plan to start the party around four in the afternoon, before people leave for the weekend.
